short: Pioneering feminist philosopher whose writings demanded fundamental educational and social equality.
full:
Mary Wollstonecraft lived a radically independent life as a writer and intellectual during a period of profound social upheaval sparked by the French Revolution. In 1792, she published A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, a searing critique of the prevailing view that women were naturally intellectually inferior and existed merely to please men.

She argued passionately that women appeared inferior only because they were denied equal access to education, demanding that women be treated as rational beings capable of full citizenship and financial independence. Although her reputation was temporarily scandalised after her premature death from childbirth fever, her work laid the crucial philosophical groundwork for the modern women's rights movement.
